newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: About 3,000 Zairean refugees arrive in Zambia.
newsitem.headline: About 3,000 Zairean refugees arrive in Zambia.

text.p: About 3,000 people fleeing fighting in Zaire arrived in neighbouring Zambia on barges across Lake Tanganyika overnight, the Zambia Red Cross said on Friday.
It said another 3,000 were expected in northern Zambia on Friday after being marooned on the lake on Thursday when their barges ran out of fuel.
"We have just received information that around 3,000 Zairean refugees arrived in the country last night," Zambia Red Cross secretary general Chipo Lungu told Reuters.
"We are still awaiting the arrival of about 3,000 others, whom we understand were marooned on the lake after running out of fuel," she added.
The refugees were headed for Zambia in four barges, she said.
Lungu said the new arrivals crossed the border at Mpulungu in north Zambia where they were met by officials from the Red Cross and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
The UNHCR said about 5,300 Zaireans had so far crossed the border since October 1996, including those that arrived on Thursday.

Zairean rebels started their campaign in October accusing the authorities of denying them citizenship. Fighting has slowly intensified with the rebels capturing a swath of territory and blunting a government army counter-offensive.

The UNHCR said about 1,000 refugees have been accommodated at the Maheba refugee camp in Zambia's northwestern Solwezi dsitrict. A further 300 are waiting to be transferred to the camp and are being housed in a community hall in Mpulungu. The rest are still on the barges that brought them to Zambia.
The U.N. said soldiers were among the refugees fleeing Zaire. Eight arrived with a group of refugees last week.
The Zambian government has increased police, soldiers and immigration officials on the border with Zaire to ensure proper screening of Zaireans crossing over.
